01 · The solution
ROM · Rough order of magnitude · budget guidance only · not an offer
— The brief

Small footprint.
32 destinations.

A sorter with 32 divert destinations fed from a single 5 m infeed, in the smallest practical footprint. The arrangement here is Orion's standard straight double-sided Helix line, sized to that brief.

Key figures (indicative)

Footprint about 40.5 x 9.5 m including cage positions
Belt width 850 mm · Line speed 1.0 m/s
Helix banks 16, each 5 x 200 mm modules (80 modules)
Bank pitch 2.1 m · Destinations 32 takeaways, 2 cage positions each

Helix swivel-wheel divertsHeliOSOrion controlsCE / UKCA
— How it works

Induct. Operators place items onto a short gravity decant at the head of the 5 m infeed.

Gap. Three gapping belts, each running faster than the last, open a gap between consecutive items.

Scan. An overhead scan arch over the last 1.5 m of the infeed reads each label. From here every item is tracked to its destination.

Divert. 16 Helix banks of steerable blue swivel wheels turn each item 30° to the left or right onto its takeaway.

Clear. Takeaways carry items to an end table with a stack light, beside two cage positions. Unread or unassigned items run off the end of the line into the kickout.

— Concept general arrangement · ORI-TST-LAY-032 Rev A

The layout.

Flow is left to right. Odd-numbered destinations divert north, even-numbered south. Dimensions are indicative, drawn without a site drawing; the arrangement is fitted to the building once a site layout is available.

Concept GA, not to construction tolerance · cages shown as positions only
Throughput basis

~5,500 items/h at 1.0 m/s, assuming a 400 mm mean item length and a 250 mm minimum gap. To be confirmed against the actual item profile.

More destinations

Each further pair of destinations adds one Helix bank and 2.1 m of spine. Throughput is set by the infeed and gap, not by the number of diverts.

Item envelope

Proven in live operation up to 30 kg and 1,200 x 1,000 x 600 mm. A smaller maximum item allows a shorter bank.

04 · Helix
ROM · Rough order of magnitude · budget guidance only · not an offer
— Orion's own sorter

Steerable wheels.
A 200 mm gap.

Helix diverts on rows of blue swivel wheels. Each wheel is driven by a 48 V DC encoder motor and steered through a mechanical linkage. Each bank turns an item left or right through 30° onto its takeaway.

Helix sorts with a gap of 200 mm between items, where many divert types need a gap of more than one item length. A smaller gap means more items per metre of belt at the same line speed.

Designed and built

Mechanics, controls and software by Orion, in West Sussex.

Modular

200 mm modules. A bank is sized to the largest item, not to a fixed product.

Helix wheel deck
Scan and tracking ahead of the sort banks

— The warehouse operating system

Run the sorter from HeliOS.

HeliOS is Orion's operating system for the warehouse floor: sort plans, flow, people, maintenance and the sorter itself, in one place. It is configured by the operator, not rewritten by a contractor.

Subscription · Core
£1,500 / month

Excl. VAT, from handover. In addition to the ROM figure.

Sort plans

Assign routes to the 32 destinations and change them between shifts without a software change.

Item traceability

Search any label read at the scan arch and see when it was sorted and to which destination.

Live operations

Items per hour, read rate, kickout rate and uptime, live or over any period.

Faults, located

A live model of the line shows where a stop is, by device and code.

07 · Basis and next steps
ROM · Rough order of magnitude · budget guidance only · not an offer
— What this ROM assumes
  • Straight double-sided line as drawn: 5 m infeed, 16 Helix banks, 32 takeaways, end-of-line kickout.
  • 850 mm belt width, 1.0 m/s, items up to 30 kg and 1,200 x 1,000 x 600 mm.
  • Overhead label scan. Dimensioning and in-motion weighing are not included.
  • Short powered takeaways with end tables and stack lights; guarding around the infeed and gapping section only.
  • Single installation visit on a clear floor, normal working hours.
  • One Orion control panel; interface to the customer WMS / sort file by a standard file or API exchange.
— Exclusions
  • Roll cages, building and civils works, mezzanines, power and data drops, fire alarm works.
  • Removal of existing equipment. HeliOS subscription (charged monthly).
— To fix the price

Item profile. Size, weight and mix of the items, and the peak hourly volume.

Site. A site drawing showing the sort area, the infeed position and the column grid.

Destinations. Confirm 32 destinations and what each one discharges to (cage, bag, chute or table).

Scan and data. Label types, and whether dimension and weight capture are needed.

How to pay. Outright, monthly, or pay per parcel.
